problem: The HTTP PD router withheld Decode output until the entire Prefill response completed, coupling first-content delivery to delayed Prefill transfer-completion polling.

change.release_condition: First complete content/reasoning/tool-call/finish SSE, or successful full Prefill completion; headers, comments and role-only SSE do not independently release while Prefill is pending.
change.prefill_accounting: Reservation lives in the Prefill future until full response consumption, failure or cancellation.
change.terminal_condition: Hold Decode [DONE] until Prefill succeeds. A late error terminates the body with an error.
change.cancellation: Response-body closure cancels pending upstream work even while Decode is idle.
change.unchanged: Model computation, generated bytes/order, PD topology, numerical kernels, sampling, official AIPerf command, nonstream behavior and logprob merging.

rule_review.basis: Q1 permits configuring/patching serving stacks without changing what the model computes; Optimization Guidelines allow routing and scheduling. Patches must be submitted for judge review.
rule_review.assessment: This output-preserving gateway scheduling change falls within the published Basic permissions. This is an interpretation of the published rules, not an individual organizer approval.

validation.toolchain: rustc/cargo 1.95.0, locked Cargo.lock, offline local CPU build

regression_on_old_code.expected_failure: Valid Decode content could not release the response while Prefill headers were withheld.

image_provenance_fixtures.purpose: Accept matching patch metadata and reject stale/missing router patch, no-delay patch, and Cargo.lock identities.

coverage: early output with Prefill headers withheld
exact forwarded bytes including fragmented UTF-8 and CRLF
role/comment-only output is not early success
fragmented terminal SSE held pending Prefill
Prefill status/truncation errors before and after first content
client cancellation before and after first content
idle Decode cancellation when Prefill finishes first
nonstream barrier and actual logprob merge

launch_preflight.full_python_suite: Completed locally; 3 macOS tool/path failures passed after GNU tar and short temporary paths. Four existing tests require Linux /proc boot_id and are deferred to the mandatory Linux Actions validation before build/GPU.

evidence.identity_limit: No per-request mapping between client request_id and SGLang rid/room is present in the archived exports. Count-curve shifts are not individual request latency measurements.
prior_corrections: Optimistic bootstrap overlaps waiting/forward; summing all logged Prefill durations double-counts time.
Earlier ~470ms page-retention and ~30ms DMA estimates cannot be recovered from those fields.
Stock router 0.3.2 also awaited the full Prefill body; the earlier load-lifetime patch did not introduce this dependency.

performance.reason: User authorized one normal benchmark on 2026-10-28 to measure TTFT, ITL, response completion and official score. No Nsight/profile capture or repeated kernel selection.

sla_sensitivity.assumption: Each first content arrives earlier by a uniform assumed amount, while response completion time, token count and request schedule stay fixed. Actual per-request router waiting is unknown. These are sensitivity cases, not measured gains/losses or official scores.

performance.verified_metric_identity: For every archived profiling request, decode_duration = request_latency - time_to_first_token and inter_token_latency = decode_duration/(output_sequence_length-1), to floating-point precision.

rollout.adoption: Candidate only. Faster first-content delivery does not establish a goodput gain; existing-log sensitivity shows that a longer measured decode interval can create additional ITL violations.
